an5.77:1.1: “Monks, these five future dangers are just enough, when considered, for a monk living in the wilderness—heedful, ardent, & resolute—to live for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.
an5.77:2.2: “There is the case where a monk living in the wilderness reminds himself of this:
an5.77:2.3: ‘I am now living alone in the wilderness.
an5.77:2.4: While I am living alone in the wilderness,
an5.77:2.5: a snake might bite me, a scorpion might sting me, a centipede might bite me.
an5.77:2.6: That would be how my death would come about. That would be an obstruction for me.
an5.77:2.7: So let me make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.’
an5.77:2.8: “This is the first future danger that is just enough, when considered, for a monk living in the wilderness—heedful, ardent, & resolute—to live for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.
an5.77:3.1: “And further, the monk living in the wilderness reminds himself of this:
an5.77:3.2: ‘I am now living alone in the wilderness.
an5.77:3.3: While I am living alone in the wilderness,
an5.77:3.4: stumbling, I might fall; my food, digested, might trouble me; my bile might be provoked, my phlegm… piercing wind forces (in the body) might be provoked.
an5.77:3.5: That would be how my death would come about. That would be an obstruction for me.
an5.77:3.6: So let me make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.’
an5.77:3.7: “This is the second future danger that is just enough, when considered, for a monk living in the wilderness—heedful, ardent, & resolute—to live for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.
an5.77:4.1: “And further, the monk living in the wilderness reminds himself of this:
an5.77:4.2: ‘I am now living alone in the wilderness.
an5.77:4.3: While I am living alone in the wilderness,
an5.77:4.4: I might meet up with vicious beasts: a lion or a tiger or a leopard or a bear or a hyena. They might take my life.
an5.77:4.5: That would be how my death would come about. That would be an obstruction for me.
an5.77:4.6: So let me make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.’
an5.77:4.7: “This is the third future danger that is just enough, when considered, for a monk living in the wilderness—heedful, ardent, & resolute—to live for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.
an5.77:5.1: “And further, the monk living in the wilderness reminds himself of this:
an5.77:5.2: ‘I am now living alone in the wilderness.
an5.77:5.3: While I am living alone in the wilderness,
an5.77:5.4: I might meet up with youths on their way to committing a crime or on their way back. They might take my life.
an5.77:5.5: That would be how my death would come about. That would be an obstruction for me.
an5.77:5.6: So let me make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.’

an5.77:6.1: “And further, the monk living in the wilderness reminds himself of this:
an5.77:6.2: ‘I am now living alone in the wilderness.
an5.77:6.3: And in the wilderness are vicious non-human beings [spirits]. They might take my life.
an5.77:6.4: That would be how my death would come about. That would be an obstruction for me.
an5.77:6.5: So let me make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.’
